title: Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen: Masterpieces
subtitle: Mirrors, journeys and imagined landscapes test the rules by which pictures make sense.
introduction:
Magritte's mirror makes one obvious mistake and one crucially correct reflection. The man's face remains unavailable, but the book behaves normally. A small portion of dependable space makes the larger impossibility harder to dismiss. Other works in this selection unsettle expectations less abruptly: an immense tower dwarfs its builders, a traveller looks back rather than ahead, and a waterfall takes shape from a narrow range of tones.

The common question is how much information a picture needs to persuade. Drawings can leave paper open; a portrait can dispense with a narrative; a landscape can make a tiny settlement sufficient to establish the scale of an entire terrain.

books.title: Dutch Paintings in The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Volumes I and II
books.author: Walter Liedtke
books.note: Walter Liedtke's Dutch Paintings in The Metropolitan Museum of Art supplies detailed context for the landscapes, portraits and domestic scenes in the middle of this selection. It is particularly useful for comparing the aims of different seventeenth-century genres.

works.title: The Wayfarer
works.credit: The wayfarer. WikiArt; Hieronymus Bosch. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The traveller's body carries on while his attention turns back. Bosch makes that divided direction the first problem of the image. The pack and stick identify a journey, but the building, dog and scattered objects complicate its immediate surroundings. Before assigning every detail a fixed moral meaning, follow how the glance interrupts a straightforward movement away.

works.title: Saint Christopher
works.credit: Saint Christopher. WikiArt; Hieronymus Bosch. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The staff and leaning body make Christopher's crossing look laborious even before its religious meaning is considered. The child occupies a small area but gives the saint his burden. Bosch surrounds this clear action with a much less easily exhausted landscape. The central task remains intelligible while smaller incidents keep the world from becoming a simple illustration of it.

works.title: Not to Be Reproduced
works.credit: René Magritte. Not to be Reproduced. Image: WikiArt. Copyright protected (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The mirror repeats the back of Edward James's head instead of revealing his face. Its treatment of the book is ordinary, however, so the room does not follow one consistent impossible rule. Magritte supplies a recognisable portrait setting and denies its expected reward. More looking will not bring the face into view; the obstruction is built into the image.

works.title: Beach View
works.credit: Johan Hendrik Weissenbruch. Beach view. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/johan-hendrik-weissenbruch/beach-view-1891
works.description: The carts measure a beach with few fixed landmarks. One occupies the nearer wet sand; another recedes towards the water, making the intervening openness easier to judge. Weissenbruch gives considerable space to the pale sky without losing the ground beneath it. A modest moving subject can establish scale more efficiently than a detailed architectural boundary.

works.title: Lyrical
works.credit: Wassily Kandinsky. Lyrical (Lyrics). WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/wassily-kandinsky/lyrical-lyrics-1911
works.description: The suggestion of horse and rider remains available, though much of the setting has fallen away. Long lines carry the action across scattered coloured areas. Kandinsky leaves the subject near the threshold of recognition: the marks can be read as movement through a place or as a movement occurring within the painted surface itself.

works.title: Port de Javel
works.credit: Port de Javel. WikiArt; Paul Gauguin. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Boats, low buildings and smoke belong to a working riverside, while the extensive clouds make weather an equally substantial part of the view. Gauguin lets industrial activity occupy an intelligible landscape rather than separating it into an emblem of modernity. The scene is useful in its own right, not only as a preliminary to the painter's later work.

works.title: Rotterdam Harbour
works.credit: Rotterdam Harbour. WikiArt; Paul Signac. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The cranes and sails have to be recognised through a surface of small coloured touches. Signac gives machinery and water a shared handling without pretending that they are the same material. Distance softens the far bank, while the active colour remains close to the eye. The harbour's industrial identity survives its transformation into a luminous pattern.

works.title: Two Male Heads
works.credit: Hieronymus Bosch. Two Male Heads. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/hieronymus-bosch/two-male-heads
works.description: The heads stand close enough for differences of glance and expression to become the principal event. Elaborate head coverings add another set of comparisons within the narrow field. With little surrounding narrative to explain them, the faces remain particular but not fully accounted for. Proximity produces a relationship without establishing exactly what the men think of each other.

works.title: The Château of Nègrepelisse
works.credit: Castle Nègrepeliss. WikiArt; Jean-Honoré Fragonard. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Much of the paper remains available around the warm drawing marks. Fragonard can therefore suggest a substantial building without giving every wall an equally closed boundary. Towers and surrounding terrain emerge through selective description. The economy is instructive: an image can make a site comprehensible while preserving the openness of an initial encounter with it.

works.title: The Resurrection of Christ
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Resurrection of Christ. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pieter-bruegel-the-elder/the-resurrection-of-christ
works.description: The upright Christ contrasts with the soldiers' disrupted poses around the tomb. Bruegel organises the religious event through different bodily directions, concentrating the drawing below while keeping the rising figure clear. The separation makes the subject readable amid its detail. Stability and disturbance are assigned to different parts of the same scene.

works.title: The Little Tower of Babel
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The "Little" Tower of Babel. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The tower is graspable as a repeated pattern of arches before its enormous size becomes fully apparent. The small city and river then supply the comparison that makes it overwhelming. Bruegel leaves the upper levels unfinished, so the structure is also an activity still in progress. Its architectural order cannot guarantee that the undertaking will succeed.

works.title: Abraham and the Three Angels
works.credit: Arent de Gelder. Abraham and three Angels. Image credit: Sailko. Wikimedia Commons. CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The visitors and their host meet around food, giving a divine encounter the arrangement of hospitality. De Gelder lets faces and fabric emerge from a subdued setting rather than announcing the event through an expansive spectacle. The shared table joins the figures, while their separate responses keep the gathering from becoming one undifferentiated expression of reverence.

works.title: Anglers on a Small Wooden Bridge
works.catalogueTitle: Anglers on a Small Wooden Bridge
works.credit: Maerten Fransz. van der Hulst. Anglers on a Small Wooden Bridge. Image credit: Maerten Fransz. van der Hulst. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The bridge provides a firm set of angles against a softer landscape. The anglers lean from that structure, giving its practical purpose a visible human scale. Van der Hulst allows a small pastime to organise a broad view. Water, distant land and sky can remain open because the nearer crossing has already established a place from which to look.

works.title: A Small Courtyard
works.credit: Esaias Boursse. Binnenplaatsje. Image credit: Sailko. Wikimedia Commons. CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Brick walls contain a limited working space, but Boursse differentiates its surfaces rather than treating the enclosure as a single dull background. Cloth, wood and masonry answer the light differently. The bent worker belongs within those practical surroundings. The courtyard acquires specificity from use and material, without needing an exceptional event to justify the picture.

works.title: A Woman Spinning
works.credit: Gerard ter Borch. A Woman Spinning. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The distance between the hands is small, yet it explains the task. Pale cuffs and collar recover the working figure from the dark room, leaving less relevant surroundings indistinct. Ter Borch makes attention proportionate to the activity: a movement of thread deserves closer description than the larger space that happens to contain it.

works.title: Head of a Cow
works.credit: Dirck Govertsz. Head of a Cow. Image credit: Dirck Govertsz. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The frontal head adopts a format familiar from human portraiture, but the horns and curling forelock make its proportions unmistakably animal. Unequal light prevents the symmetry from becoming rigid. The close view gives texture and small asymmetries unusual consequence. Individual presence does not depend here on an expressive gesture or a narrative setting.

works.title: Head of Christ
works.credit: Dieric Bouts. Head of Christ. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/dirk-bouts/head-of-christ
works.description: There is no crowd or event to follow. The frontal face and near symmetry concentrate the devotional image into a sustained address, with dark hair and background framing the pale features. Bouts limits the means of distraction. The painting's directness comes from that restriction, quite unlike the crowded religious narratives elsewhere in this selection.

works.title: Rjukanfossen
works.credit: Peder Balke. Rjukanfossen. Image credit: Peder Balke; Source credit: Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Dark rock gives the pale falling water its force. Balke needs only a narrow tonal range to distinguish resistant surfaces from mist and dispersed spray. The contrast makes a large landscape readable without exhaustive detail. Notice where a mark ceases to describe a particular stone and begins to carry the general instability of the water beside it.

works.title: A River Valley with a Group of Houses
works.catalogueTitle: A River Valley with a Group of Houses
works.credit: Hercules Seghers. A River Valley with a Group of Houses. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The houses offer a recognisable scale beneath the rocky height. Strong differences between the darker foreground and pale distance make the valley extend beyond that small settlement. Seghers lets habitation provide a foothold within terrain that can otherwise feel difficult to measure. The buildings do not dominate the view; they make its magnitude interpretable.

works.title: Judith with the Head of Holofernes
works.catalogueTitle: Judith with the Head of Holofernes
works.credit: Gerrit Pietersz Sweelink. Judith with the Head of Holofernes. Image credit: Gerrit Pietersz Sweelink. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The severed head is held low, leaving more space for the women's faces and contrasting ages. Sweelinck gives the aftermath its own subject rather than reconstructing the act of killing. Drapery and shadow concentrate the pair, but their expressions need not be translated into a single assured emotion. The completed deed remains present as a physical object between them.

closingSections.title: Check the work's location separately
paragraphs: Boijmans's collection records, Depot presentations and loans should not be treated as one permanent hanging. Check the museum's current location and access information for any work you want to see. For reading online, compare Magritte's withheld face with the directness of the *Head of Christ*: each makes visibility itself consequential.
